title: Decomposition
description: Output of the Decomposer agent: a DAG of work items that together achieve the outcome. Reviewed by a human at Gate 1 before any specification is written.

revision.description: Incremented each time the decomposer re-runs after human feedback.

summary.description: Plain-language narrative of the approach, written for the business owner. Should be readable in under two minutes.

coverage.description: Maps every success metric from the outcome to the work items that move it. A metric with no work items is a gap the human must see.

explicitly_out_of_scope.description: Things a reasonable reader might expect but that are deliberately not included, with the reason.

kind.description: feature = user-visible capability; task = internal engineering change; workflow = multi-step business process to automate; agent = an LLM agent to be built; spike = time-boxed investigation that produces a decision, not code; migration = data/schema/infra move.

intent.description: What this item achieves for the outcome, in one paragraph. Not how.

depends_on.description: work_item_ids that must be merged first. Must form a DAG.

size.description: The band of estimated_lines under the run's size budget (default XS ≤ 50, S ≤ 150, M ≤ 400). L is above M and must be split.

estimated_lines.description: Estimated hand-written changed lines, tests included, generated files excluded (linguist-generated in .gitattributes, lockfiles, files regenerated by a named command). Post-mortem 2026-10-11 §3.

regenerates.description: Generated files this item rewrites with a named command. A refresh that rewrites a large generated file is its own item that lands first, unless it is small.

paths.description: Globs of the files the command rewrites.

command.description: The repository command that regenerates them, e.g. `bun run catalog:refresh`.

human_judgement_required.description: True when the item involves a product, legal, pricing, or UX decision the owner must make. Such items get a mandatory clarification before specification.
